rationale: ⚠️ Connection status is serialized and parsed as a scalar enum. The contract mistakenly references the aggregate status object instead of the scalar connectivity status schema.
⚠️ The accepted widget schema explicitly exposes description, but mapping targets and persistence contain no corresponding field. The implementation cannot preserve that documented widget data.

⚠️ The required query input is documented consistently, including the method annotation. Its parameter lacks the runtime QueryParam binding, so the implementation binds the unannotated value as an entity.
⚠️ The slug parameter explicitly filters organization slugs, but its equality condition uses name. The implementation substitutes the wrong input.
⚠️ The environment context reaches the lookup, but a successful global ID lookup bypasses environment matching. The implementation can return a category outside the selected environment.
⚠️ The route supplies projectName, while the GET handler requires projectId. This inconsistent runtime path binding prevents the documented operation from resolving its project.
⚠️ The DELETE handler requests projectId although its route binds projectName. The implementation's required path-variable name is inconsistent with the registered route.
⚠️ The user controller and bulk handler consistently delete users by user ID. The annotation's reference to launches is an incorrect operation description.
⚠️ MQTT 5 is an explicit supported connection type and is serialized by the normal retrieval path. The contract enumeration omits this implemented domain value.
⚠️ The operation describes tokens in the plural and deliberately returns a DAO list. The response annotation omits its collection container, incorrectly describing a single token.
⚠️ Rejecting an invalid report UUID as a bad request is consistent with explicit validation and shared HTTP mapping. The contract's response list omits that client-error outcome.
⚠️ The project-scoped export passes only launchId to a global lookup. The export handler never verifies the launch belongs to the selected project, violating route scoping.
⚠️ The collection serializes connection domain types directly, and that domain explicitly includes mqtt-5. The contract's enumeration is incomplete.

⚠️ Both registered routing and handler documentation consistently use manifests. The contract's singular manifest path appears to be a documentation error, although no history confirms which spelling was originally intended.
⚠️ The stored terms-of-service domain explicitly includes version 2 and the JSON getter returns that enum. The response schema has not included the supported additional value.

⚠️ Deletion receives the environment context but globally resolves categoryId and deletes without matching the category's environment. The implementation fails to enforce the selected environment's scope.

⚠️ The request exposes townName while the domain address stores city. The mapper declares no translation between these differently named properties, losing the submitted town during payment initiation.

⚠️ The targeted shape mismatch comes from the single-Token annotation despite a deliberate list return. The separate Quay DAO selection is also suspicious but does not justify documenting the response as one token.

⚠️ Merge-patch authorization deliberately checks unrestricted WRITE on every affected leaf when root permission is partial. The contract overstates the requirement by excluding this explicit, resource-scoped authorization path.
⚠️ Metadata has an explicit JSON-object field definition and object serialization. The response schema's string type is inconsistent with the structured metadata model.
⚠️ The domain can read and retain allowedImportAdditions, and the request schema permits it. The PUT-specific reconstruction drops that property instead of passing it into the supported domain model.
⚠️ The connection model reads and writes scalar connectivity status names. The schema incorrectly references the separate aggregate connection-status object for this scalar field.
⚠️ User retrieval returns the stored enum through its JSON getter, and that enum intentionally includes TOS_VERSION_2. The response schema omits a supported terms-of-service version.
⚠️ The documented slug filter has its own supplied value, but the implementation builds slug equality from name. The wrong variable causes incorrect project filtering.

⚠️ Update accepts widget descriptions through the documented schema, but neither mapped domain widgets nor persisted widgets can store them. The implementation drops an explicitly supported input field.

⚠️ The contract explicitly promises a created-instance ID object. The handler discards the creation result and constructs success without attaching a payload, leaving that documented output unpopulated.
⚠️ The shared error serializer deliberately wraps errors in an object, and this handler uses that shared response path. The contract's bare-array definition misdescribes the common error envelope.

⚠️ Omitted attributes are allowed at the controller boundary, but content loading passes the nullable array directly to Lists.newArrayList. The implementation fails to supply an empty default or handle the omitted input.
⚠️ Payment information maps an address with city into the response schema's townName. No mapping bridges the different property names, so the implementation omits documented address information.
⚠️ The trailing-slash route binds projectName, while its handler requires projectKey. This runtime binding mismatch prevents the promised successful preference retrieval.

⚠️ Instance deletion sends failures through the shared serializer, which explicitly creates an errors object envelope. The contract's top-level array definition does not describe that established response representation.

⚠️ The operation patches the features collection and its path contains only thingId. Requiring featureId as another path parameter is internally inconsistent; the implementation correctly handles the collection body at path end.

⚠️ Membership identifies the selected project, but bulk update checks only that project exists before globally loading item IDs. It changes item descriptions without confirming those items belong to the selected project.

⚠️ The nested route identifies a user's key, but deletion ignores userId and uses global key existence alone. The implementation does not enforce the parent-child association represented by its route.
⚠️ The response schema explicitly declares an object identifying the removed instance. Although the handler has the instance ID, its success responder never receives that promised payload.
⚠️ Collection retrieval serializes selected Thing fields through the object-valued metadata definition. The contract incorrectly describes that structured field as a string.
